Should earth climate models be able to accurately back-cast ?

Any good model can (or should be able to) predict and back-predict anything. However, there's really no point in trying to "back-cast" our climate, since we can directly measure global carbon dioxide levels for the last few thousand years, and therefore, very accurately infer past average temperatures from that.

But if you were to "back-cast" climate models, your model would need to include many, MANY factors/variables, such as the earth's population, pollution rates, CO2 levels, deforestation rates, and probably many other things, all as a function of time, and all in reverse.
